authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Crocs recorded non-cash impairments in 2025 on the HEYDUDE trademark ($430.0 million) and HEYDUDE reporting unit goodwill ($307.0 million), part of total asset impairments of $738.1 million. The triggering event came from lower HEYDUDE forecasts in the second quarter of 2025.
The Board increased the share repurchase authorization by $1.5 billion, leaving approximately $2.0 billion available for repurchase.

Following the Supreme Court's IEEPA tariff ruling and the Court of International Trade's refund order, Crocs had received about $67 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, including interest. About $64 million was booked as a benefit in cost of sales in the third quarter. Management calls the refunds non-recurring.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 7 business descriptions
business_model.claim: Crocs, Inc. designs, markets, distributes and sells casual lifestyle footwear and accessories. Its products are built around the Crocs clog, sandals and Jibbitz charms, and the HEYDUDE loafer.
quotes: casual lifestyle footwear and accessories for all

business_model.claim: The company reports two segments, the Crocs Brand and the HEYDUDE Brand. In FY2025 the Crocs Brand produced $3,325,807 of revenues and HEYDUDE 714,840 (table in thousands).
quotes: We have two reportable operating segments: the Crocs Brand and the HEYDUDE Brand

business_model.claim: Products are sold in more than 85 countries through two channels, wholesale and direct-to-consumer. In 2025 the DTC share of consolidated revenues was 52.1%, up from 49.7% in 2024, and the wholesale share was 47.9%.
quotes: through two distribution channels: wholesale and direct-to-consumer

business_model.claim: Wholesale customers are multi-brand retailers, mono-branded partner stores, e-tailers and distributors. DTC sales go through company-operated e-commerce sites, third-party marketplaces and company-operated stores.
quotes: Our wholesale channel includes domestic and international multi-brand retailers, mono-branded partner stores, e-tailers, and distributors.

business_model.claim: Revenue moves with unit volume, average selling price and currency. In Q3 2026 revenues rose 4.6%, with higher unit volume adding $37.6 million (3.8%) and higher average selling price adding $9.0 million (0.9%).
quotes: higher unit sales volume in both brands, which resulted in an increase in revenues of $37.6 million, or 3.8%

business_model.claim: Within the Crocs Brand, DTC is the faster-growing channel. In Q3 2026 Crocs Brand DTC revenue grew 8.2% while Crocs Brand wholesale changed by (0.5)%.
HEYDUDE revenue fell 13.3% in FY2025, mainly on lower volume and a 26.3% drop in wholesale. It then grew 6.1% in Q3 2026.
quotes: HEYDUDE Brand revenues increased 6.1%, or 6.2% on a constant currency basis

business_model.claim: Margins differ by brand. In FY2025 the Crocs Brand gross margin was 61.3% and the HEYDUDE gross margin was 44.8%.
quotes: Gross margin was 44.8% for the year ended December 31, 2025

business_model.claim: All footwear is made by third-party manufacturers outside the U.S., mostly in Vietnam, China, Indonesia, India and Mexico, so product cost, duties and freight are the main cost-of-sales drivers.
quotes: All of our footwear products are manufactured by third-party manufacturers, the majority of which are located in Vietnam, China, Indonesia, India, and Mexico.

business_model.claim: Tariffs and freight were the main reasons FY2025 gross margin fell to 58.3% from 58.8%, with incremental duties costing 130 basis points and freight and fulfillment 40.
quotes: This was primarily due to incremental duties of 130 basis points and higher freight and fulfillment costs of 40 basis points, for both brands.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release
business_model.claim: Q3 2026 gross margin of 66.2% was lifted by one-time IEEPA tariff refunds, with about $64 million booked in cost of sales, worth 630 basis points. The company calls these refunds non-recurring.
quotes: These refunds are non-recurring.

business_model.claim: SG&A is the other main cost line. It reached 38.2% of revenues in Q3 2026, with the increase attributed mainly to higher DTC costs of $9.2 million.
quotes: primarily due to higher DTC costs of $9.2 million, driven by increased share of marketplaces and rent expense as a result of investments in the channel

business_model.basis: store counts stated in 10-K Item 1; cost behavior stated in 10-K risk factors
business_model.claim: The company runs 514 company-operated stores, 439 for the Crocs Brand and 75 for HEYDUDE as of December 31, 2025. The company notes these stores carry higher fixed costs than e-commerce.
quotes: we may not be able to profitably operate existing retail stores, due to the higher fixed costs associated with our retail business compared to e-commerce distribution

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q cash flow statement
business_model.claim: The business generates cash well above capital needs. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow was 561,189 against 53,615 of capital spending and 506,194 of share repurchases (table in thousands).

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 7 business descriptions
competitive_position.claim: The company competes through two brands, Crocs Brand and HEYDUDE, sold through wholesale and direct-to-consumer channels in more than 85 countries.
quotes: We have two reportable operating segments: the Crocs Brand and the HEYDUDE Brand

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and income statement
competitive_position.claim: Momentum is positive in the latest quarter: Q3 2026 revenues were $1,042,583 (table in thousands) against $996,301 a year earlier, up 4.6%, with Crocs Brand up 4.4% and HEYDUDE up 6.1%.
quotes: Crocs Brand revenues increased by 4.4% on a reported and constant currency basis, compared to the same period in 2025.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-Q revenue-by-channel table; the mechanism is inferred from the channel-mix commentary
competitive_position.claim: Crocs Brand growth is led by direct-to-consumer, while wholesale is flat to down: Q3 DTC revenues grew 8.2% and wholesale changed (0.5)%; over nine months DTC grew 11.1% and wholesale changed (4.3)%.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-K and the earnings release
competitive_position.claim: International expansion is part of the Crocs Brand position: international sales were 48.6% of Crocs Brand revenues in 2025, up from 44.1% in 2024, and management described double-digit international growth in Q3 2026.
quotes: Our international sales in 2025 were 48.6% of Crocs Brand revenues compared to 44.1% and 41.0% in 2024 and 2023, respectively.
led by double-digit international revenue growth

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release reconciliation
competitive_position.claim: Reported Q3 gross margin was 66.2% against 58.5%, but part of the gain came from tariff refunds of 630 basis points that the company calls non-recurring; adjusted gross margin was 60.3%.
quotes: These refunds are non-recurring.

competitive_position.claim: There is some evidence of pricing support in Q3: higher ASP added $9.0 million, or 0.9%, to revenues, driven by increased pricing in both brands, and unit volume added $37.6 million, or 3.8%.
quotes: higher ASP of $9.0 million, or 0.9%, driven by increased pricing in both brands

competitive_position.basis: stated in the earnings release; the adjustments are company-defined non-GAAP measures
competitive_position.claim: Adjusted operating margin rose to 22.3% from 20.8% in Q3 2026, so underlying profitability improved year over year.
quotes: Adjusted income from operations of $232 million increased 11.7% from $208 million, resulting in adjusted operating margin of 22.3% compared to 20.8%.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cash flow statement; the funding link is inferred
competitive_position.claim: The business generates cash that funds brand investment and buybacks: nine-month operating cash flow was 561,189 against capital spending of 53,615 and share repurchases of 506,194 (table in thousands).
quotes: we returned $250 million to shareholders through share repurchases while continuing to strengthen our balance sheet through debt paydown

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and balance sheet
competitive_position.claim: Financial capacity is large but debt-financed: liquidity included $901.4 million of available borrowing capacity and total borrowings were $1.3 billion at September 30, 2026.
quotes: Our liquidity position remains strong with $163.5 million in cash and cash equivalents and $901.4 million in available borrowing capacity as of September 30, 2026.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A, 10-Q MD&A and earnings release
competitive_position.claim: HEYDUDE is the weaker brand. In 2025 its revenues fell 13.3% and the company recorded asset impairments of $738.1 million, mostly on the HEYDUDE trademark and goodwill. It returned to growth of 6.1% in Q3 2026, though nine-month revenues are still (4.3)% lower.
quotes: HEYDUDE Brand Returns To Growth With Revenues Up 6% To Prior Year

competitive_position.basis: stated guidance in the earnings release; it is a management expectation, not an outcome
competitive_position.claim: Management's 2026 outlook was raised to revenues up approximately 3%, signalling confidence in the brands' current position.
quotes: Revenues to be up approximately 3% compared to full year 2025

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factors and MD&A
competitive_position.claim: Named threat, competition and pricing pressure: the company says the footwear industry is highly competitive, that many competitors have greater resources, and that a highly promotional environment could force price cuts and lower margins.
quotes: The footwear industry is highly competitive.
The overall increase in Crocs Brand revenues was offset in part by lower ASP, mainly due to increased discounting, partially offset by favorable channel mix.

competitive_position.claim: Named threat, tariffs and product cost: duties that remain in effect continue to raise product costs, and in 2025 incremental duties cost 130 basis points of gross margin. The U.S. tariffs now range from 10% to 12.5%, and the company expects $75 million to $80 million of IEEPA refunds, of which about $67 million has been received.
quotes: The tariffs that remain in effect continue to increase our product costs.

competitive_position.claim: Named threat, supply concentration: all footwear is made by third-party manufacturers outside the U.S., with about 45% of 2025 Crocs Brand production in Vietnam.
quotes: We depend solely on third-party manufacturers located outside of the U.S.

competitive_position.claim: Named threat, consumer demand and geopolitics: discretionary spending is under pressure, wholesale partners are cautious, and the Middle East conflict has reduced revenues in several distributor markets and raised raw material and transport costs.
quotes: Given this, our wholesale partners are also acting cautiously.
Most recently, the conflict in the Middle East has caused, and may continue to cause, a reduction in our revenues for several of our distributor markets

quotes: Our liquidity position remains strong with $163.5 million in cash and cash equivalents and $901.4 million in available borrowing capacity as of September 30, 2026.

financial_health.basis: Stated figures in F1; the comparison is inferred.

Debt is therefore higher than at the prior year-end and close to the size of book equity.
quotes: Our total borrowings were $1.3 billion as of September 30, 2026.

financial_health.basis: Stated in F3; the direction of change is read from the printed lines. The counter point rests on a quote from P6.

financial_health.basis: Stated figures in F2; the interpretation is inferred.

Cash generation: cash provided by operating activities was 561,189 for the nine months against 457,901 a year earlier, while purchases of property, equipment, and software were 53,615 against 45,120 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in F1, F2 and F3; the tax-timing reading is inferred from those lines.
financial_health.claim: Quality of cash flow, part 1: operating cash flow of 561,189 is close to net income of 559,198 (table in thousands). Non-cash add-backs include depreciation and amortization of 60,875 and share-based compensation of 36,496. Income taxes were an inflow of 69,303 against an outflow of (11,802) a year earlier, consistent with income taxes receivable falling to 2,918 from 32,782 and income taxes payable rising to 84,174 from 47,308.

Quality of cash flow, part 2: reported margins include non-recurring tariff refunds. About $67 million of IEEPA refunds had been received, of which about $64 million is in cost of sales and about $3 million in interest income, and the company expects $75 million to $80 million in total. Excluding the refunds, Q3 gross margin was 60.3% against the reported 66.2%.
quotes: These refunds are non-recurring.

financial_health.basis: Stated in F3, P4 and P7; the link to limited debt reduction is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Uses of cash: repurchases of common stock including excise tax were 506,194 for the nine months against 402,153 a year earlier, and cash used in financing activities was 472,532 (table in thousands). The company repurchased $250.0 million in Q3, and about $2.0 billion remains under the authorization.
quotes: The repurchase authorization does not have an expiration date and does not oblige the Company to acquire any particular amount of the Company’s common stock.

financial_health.basis: Inferred from the absence of a debt line in the current liabilities listed in F1.
financial_health.claim: Refinancing, part 1: the balance sheet shows no current portion of borrowings among current liabilities, and borrowings of 1,289,044 are all in long-term borrowings (table in thousands). No debt maturity is shown as falling due within the year, but the maturity dates themselves are not in the evidence.

financial_health.basis: Stated in P3; the latest capacity is from P4.
financial_health.claim: Refinancing, part 2: management's stated way of meeting obligations is operating cash flow, cash on hand and undrawn facilities. At the prior year-end the Term Loan B was fully drawn with no capacity, while $937.4 million was available under the Revolving Facility and $15.0 million under the Citibank Facility. Management also says additional financing may be needed and cannot be assured.
quotes: We believe that our cash flows from operations, our cash and cash equivalents on hand, and available borrowings under our Revolving Facility and Citibank Facility will be sufficient to meet our ongoing liquidity needs and capital expenditure requirements for at least the next twelve months.

Additional future financing may be necessary to fund our operations and there can be no assurance that, if needed, we will be able to secure additional debt or equity financing on terms acceptable to us or at all.

financial_health.basis: Stated in F1; its significance for cash needs is inferred.
financial_health.claim: A large non-debt liability sits on the balance sheet: long-term income taxes payable of 641,563 against 649,057 at the prior year-end (table in thousands). Its settlement timing is not shown in the evidence.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A revenue-by-channel table. The conditions are inferred from the SG&A explanation.
growth_thesis.claim: Crocs Brand direct-to-consumer (DTC) sales are a growth driver. Q3 2026 Crocs Brand DTC revenue rose 8.2% and the nine-month figure rose 11.1%, ahead of total Crocs Brand growth of 4.4% in Q3. To continue, the company must keep funding the channel and keep DTC demand strong.
quotes: Crocs Brand revenues increased by 4.4% on a reported and constant currency basis, compared to the same period in 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q table and the earnings release. The condition about wholesale is inferred from the channel split.
growth_thesis.claim: HEYDUDE returned to growth in Q3 2026, with revenues up 6.1%, after falling 4.3% over the nine months. For this to continue, the stabilization of wholesale has to hold, since HEYDUDE wholesale rose 14.0% in Q3 but is down 12.4% year to date.
quotes: HEYDUDE Brand Returns To Growth With Revenues Up 6% To Prior Year

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K and the earnings release. The conditions are inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: International expansion is a driver for the Crocs Brand. International sales were 48.6% of Crocs Brand revenues in 2025, up from 44.1% in 2024, and management cited double-digit international growth in Q3 2026. To continue, the six Tier 1 markets must keep delivering and local brand awareness must keep building.
quotes: Our international sales in 2025 were 48.6% of Crocs Brand revenues compared to 44.1% and 41.0% in 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The Crocs Brand delivered a record third quarter with revenues up 4%, led by double-digit international revenue growth and continued momentum across our product diversification strategy.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The risk is stated in the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Higher average selling price (ASP) from pricing and channel mix adds to revenue. The nine-month ASP gain was 2.9%, or $89.3 million, and Q3 ASP added 0.9%. To continue, consumers must accept price increases and unfavorable product mix must stay contained.
quotes: Revenues also increased in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to higher ASP of $89.3 million, or 2.9%, driven by favorable channel mix and increased pricing in both brands, partially offset by unfavorable product mix in both brands.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The condition is inferred from the stated trends.
growth_thesis.claim: Unit volume turned positive in Q3 2026 in both brands. It added $37.6 million, or 3.8%, to revenues, after being negative over nine months. For this to hold, consumer discretionary spending and wholesale partner orders must stay firm.
quotes: We continue to operate in an environment where consumers are feeling the effects of elevated interest rates, inflation, and future expected price increases, among other things, and as a result, there is more pressure on discretionary spending.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q and the earnings release. The condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Q3 profit growth was helped by lower tariff duties and one-time IEEPA refunds. Adjusted income from operations rose 11.7% with adjusted operating margin at 22.3% versus 20.8%, while GAAP gross margin of 66.2% was flattered by the refunds. For underlying margin gains to continue, duties must stay lower and product costs must keep falling, because the refunds will not recur.
quotes: These refunds are non-recurring.
Adjusted income from operations of $232 million increased 11.7% from $208 million, resulting in adjusted operating margin of 22.3% compared to 20.8%.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A. The comparison with SG&A is from the 10-Q.
growth_thesis.claim: Cost savings are meant to support earnings. The 10-K identified about $100 million of gross savings for 2026 after about $50 million achieved in 2025. For this to help, savings must outrun SG&A growth, which was 6.0% in Q3.
quotes: These cost reduction initiatives include approximately $50 million of gross cost savings achieved for the year ended December 31, 2025, and approximately $100 million of gross cost savings identified for 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Share counts and EPS are stated in the income statement and the 10-Q. The mechanism is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Per-share earnings are being lifted by share repurchases. Diluted weighted shares fell to 47,954 (in thousands) from 53,989 in Q3, while diluted EPS rose to $4.52 from $2.70. Continuing this requires ongoing buybacks, supported by the roughly $2.0 billion of authorization remaining.
quotes: Including this increase, approximately $2.0 billion remains available for repurchase under the Company’s common stock repurchase authorization as of the date of this Current Report on Form 8-K.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the cash flow statement and balance sheet. The dependence is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Buybacks and debt service must be funded by operating cash flow, which was 561,189 over nine months versus 457,901 a year earlier (table in thousands), against buybacks of 506,194 (table in thousands). This only continues if profits and cash conversion hold, since long-term borrowings rose to 1,289,044 (table in thousands) from 1,230,885.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release. The conditions are inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Management expects growth to continue, having raised the full-year 2026 revenue outlook to about 3% and adjusted diluted EPS to $14.45 to $14.65. For the outlook to be met, Q4 trends in both brands and the cost and tariff conditions above must hold.
quotes: Adjusted diluted earnings per share to be in the range of $14.45 to $14.65, up from our previous guidance range of $13.70 to $14.00.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A (P3) and risk factors (P2)
material_events.claim: Crocs recorded non-cash impairments in 2025 on the HEYDUDE trademark ($430.0 million) and HEYDUDE reporting unit goodwill ($307.0 million), part of total asset impairments of $738.1 million. The triggering event came from lower HEYDUDE forecasts in the second quarter of 2025.
quotes: Asset impairments were $738.1 million, primarily driven by the partial impairment of the HEYDUDE indefinite-lived trademark and HEYDUDE Brand reporting unit goodwill.

material_events.claim: The Board increased the share repurchase authorization by $1.5 billion, leaving approximately $2.0 billion available for repurchase.
quotes: On July 30, 2026, the Company also announced that its Board of Directors (the “Board”) authorized the increase of the Company’s existing common stock repurchase authorization by $1.5 billion.

quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we received approximately $67 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, including interest.

material_events.basis: stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release (P6)
material_events.claim: Crocs raised its full-year 2026 outlook on October 29, 2026. It now expects revenues up approximately 3% and adjusted diluted EPS of $14.45 to $14.65, up from $13.70 to $14.00 previously.
quotes: Adjusted diluted earnings per share to be in the range of $14.45 to $14.65, up from our previous guidance range of $13.70 to $14.00.

risks.basis: stated in P4 and P6 (refund share of margin and non-recurring label); the effect on later periods is inferred.

quotes: These refunds are non-recurring.

risks.basis: stated in P4; the cost impact on future periods is inferred.

quotes: The tariffs that remain in effect continue to increase our product costs.
While the timing remains uncertain, we currently estimate that we are eligible to receive a total of approximately $75 million to $80 million in refunds related to these tariffs, including interest.

risks.basis: stated in P2, P3 and P4 for the history and the growth figures; the risk of further impairment is inferred, since the HEYDUDE share of the remaining balances is not given.
risks.claim: HEYDUDE recovery may not hold. Revenue grew 6.1% in Q3 but is still down (4.3)% for nine months. The prior-year impairments of $430.0 million (trademark) and $307.0 million (goodwill) show how a weak forecast can trigger large write-downs.
quotes: In the past, several footwear companies, including ours, have experienced periods of rapid growth in revenues and earnings followed by periods of declining revenues and losses, and our business may be similarly affected in the future.

risks.basis: figures stated in F1, F3, P4 and P7; the funding-pressure mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: Buybacks are large relative to cash generation: repurchases of 506,194 (table in thousands) in nine months against operating cash flow of 561,189 (table in thousands), with long-term borrowings up to 1,289,044 (table in thousands) from 1,230,885 (table in thousands). A larger authorization adds scope for further debt-funded returns.
quotes: Additional future financing may be necessary to fund our operations and there can be no assurance that, if needed, we will be able to secure additional debt or equity financing on terms acceptable to us or at all.

risks.basis: stated in P4 (wholesale figures and cautionary language); the impact on later periods is inferred.

quotes: Given this, our wholesale partners are also acting cautiously.

quotes: Our effective tax rate has varied dramatically in recent years due to intra-entity intellectual property rights transactions, differences in our profitability levels and relative operating earnings across multiple jurisdictions, and by changes in the valuation allowance.

quotes: While the timing remains uncertain, we currently estimate that we are eligible to receive a total of approximately $75 million to $80 million in refunds related to these tariffs, including interest.

quotes: During the quarter, we returned $250 million to shareholders through share repurchases while continuing to strengthen our balance sheet through debt paydown.

quotes: The other relevant uncertain tax positions associated with the 2023 IP transactions remain unchanged.

quotes: Most recently, the conflict in the Middle East has caused, and may continue to cause, a reduction in our revenues for several of our distributor markets and an increase in the costs of raw materials and transportation associated with elevated oil prices.
